newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil down sharply on commercial selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil down sharply on commercial selling.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures were sharply lower at midsession on commercial selling tied to talk of heavy deliveries posted against the January, traders said.
Soymeal futures were mostly lower but cold weather supported the spot month and the January/March spread widened.
There were 1,282 lots of soyoil posted Thursday for delivery against the January and traders anticipated continued heavy deliveries.
Registration of soyoil in deliverable locations climbed by 60 lots to 4,858 lots on Wednesday, supporting talk of more deliveries against the January.
Traders said Term Commodities sold at least 400 lots March soyoil which contributed to the declines. Produce Grain reportedly sold 200 lots July soyoil.
At 1132 CST, soyoil was down 0.16 to 0.31 cent per lb with March down 0.31 at 24.45 cents.
But spot soymeal supplies remain tight and no deliveries have been posted against the January. Cash premiums remain high so traders said there was little chance of deliveries.
The latest bout of cold weather was also supportive to January soymeal as increased livestock feed demands and transportation problems added to the value of spot supplies.
Soymeal was $0.40 to $1.30 per ton lower with January down $0.40 at $240.40 and March down $1.30 at $233.50.
